cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: the inverse of the cumulative beta distribution at probability 0.685470581, alpha=8, beta=10 on [1,3]
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 2. Independently derived from the documented inverse relationship ("BETA.INV seeks that value x such that BETA.DIST(x, alpha, beta, TRUE, A, B) = probability"): A + (B-A)*betaincinv(8,10,0.685470581) = 1 + 2*0.4999999999815714 = 1.9999999999631428 -> 2 at 6 dp. The tiny shortfall comes from the input probability itself being the 9-dp rounding of BETA.DIST(2,8,10,TRUE,1,3), so 6 dp is the honest assertion depth

cases.description: The median of a Beta(2,3) distribution on the default [0,1] interval
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that omitting A and B uses the standard beta distribution on [0,1]. Independently derived: scipy.special.betaincinv(2,3,0.5) = 0.3857275681323895 -> 0.3857276 at 7 dp
Excel documents: "If probability <= 0 or probability > 1, BETA.INV returns the #NUM! error value." Note the asymmetry -- probability = 1 is allowed but probability = 0 is not
